AC9E4LA01.title: Language for Formal and Informal Relationships
AC9E4LA01.curriculum: explore language used to develop relationships in formal and informal situations

misconceptions.correction: Clarity and suitability matter more than sounding impressive.
Casual interaction still needs cooperation and audience awareness.
Relationships and purposes change language choices.
Word choice, punctuation and sentence structure also create tone.

AC9E4LA02.title: Subjective and Objective Language
AC9E4LA02.curriculum: identify the subjective language of opinion and feeling, and the objective language of factual reporting

misconceptions.correction: Selection and framing can still influence reporting; inspect evidence and sources.
Some adjectives report observable properties, such as wooden or rectangular.
A convincing evaluation explains criteria and examples.
Attribution identifies the speaker but does not verify the claim.

AC9E4LA03.title: Text Structures and Language Across the Curriculum
AC9E4LA03.curriculum: identify how texts across the curriculum have different language features and are typically organised into characteristic stages depending on purposes

misconceptions.misconception: Every subject uses one text type
misconceptions.correction: Subjects use several forms depending on the task.
Writers adapt stages while keeping purpose clear.
Use a pattern of structure and language evidence.
Headings, diagrams and captions organise and extend information.

AC9E4LA04.title: Connectives and Topic Cohesion
AC9E4LA04.curriculum: identify how text connectives including temporal and conditional words, and topic word associations are used to sequence and connect ideas

misconceptions.misconception: Any connective can join any ideas
misconceptions.correction: The connective must match the logical relationship.
Overuse can make writing mechanical or confusing.
Key terms sometimes need repeating for precision.
Check that readers can identify the noun referred to.

AC9E4LA05.title: Navigation and Readability in Online Texts
AC9E4LA05.curriculum: identify text navigation features of online texts that enhance readability including headlines, drop-down menus, links, graphics and layout

misconceptions.misconception: Navigation is only the top menu
misconceptions.correction: Headings, links, search, breadcrumbs and visual hierarchy also guide movement.
Irrelevant graphics compete with information.
Descriptive link text identifies destination and supports accessibility.

misconceptions.misconception: Desktop order automatically works on mobile
misconceptions.correction: Responsive layouts need a logical reading and focus order.

AC9E4LA06.title: Complex Sentences: Independent and Dependent Clauses
AC9E4LA06.curriculum: understand that complex sentences contain one independent clause and at least one dependent clause typically joined by a subordinating conjunction to create relationships, such as time and causality

misconceptions.misconception: A long sentence is automatically complex
misconceptions.correction: Complexity depends on clause relationships, not length.

misconceptions.misconception: Dependent clause treated as complete sentence
misconceptions.correction: It needs an independent clause unless used deliberately in dialogue or style.
It must express the intended logical relationship.
Punctuation depends on conjunction type and clause order.

AC9E4LA07.title: Quoted and Reported Speech
AC9E4LA07.curriculum: investigate how quoted (direct) and reported (indirect) speech are used

misconceptions.misconception: Reported speech copies the quotation unchanged
misconceptions.correction: Pronouns, tense and time references may need adjustment.

misconceptions.misconception: Every spoken idea needs quotation marks
misconceptions.correction: Reported speech normally uses no quotation marks around the message.
Said, claimed, admitted and promised suggest different meanings.

misconceptions.misconception: Quotation wording may be improved silently
misconceptions.correction: Direct quotation should preserve the original wording or show omissions transparently.

AC9E4LA08.title: Adverb Groups and Prepositional Phrases
AC9E4LA08.curriculum: understand how adverb groups/phrases and prepositional phrases work in different ways to provide circumstantial details about an activity

misconceptions.misconception: Every phrase beginning with -ly is required
misconceptions.correction: Many adverbs do not end in -ly, and prepositional phrases add circumstances too.
Select details that serve meaning and avoid overload.
Place the phrase where its relationship is clear.
A prepositional phrase can function adverbially, but it is still structurally a prepositional phrase.

AC9E4LA09.title: Tense and Its Impact on Meaning
AC9E4LA09.curriculum: understand past, present and future tenses and their impact on meaning in a sentence

misconceptions.misconception: Every verb in a text must use one tense
misconceptions.correction: Tense can shift when the time frame changes clearly.
English expresses future time through several constructions and context.

misconceptions.misconception: Present tense means this exact moment
misconceptions.correction: It can also express habits, general truths and narratives.
Use forms such as went, saw and wrote correctly.

AC9E4LA10.title: Framing, Placement and Salience in Images
AC9E4LA10.curriculum: explore the effect of choices when framing an image, placement of elements in the image and salience on composition of still and moving images in texts

misconceptions.correction: Placement creates emphasis; importance is constructed within the text.
Viewers use context and cultural knowledge, so claims need evidence and caution.
It can remove important context and alter interpretation.
Composition works through combinations of framing, placement, colour, focus and words.

AC9E4LA11.title: Synonyms, Antonyms and Precise Vocabulary
AC9E4LA11.curriculum: expand vocabulary by exploring a range of synonyms and antonyms, and using words encountered in a range of sources

misconceptions.correction: They differ in connotation, collocation, intensity and register.

misconceptions.misconception: Antonym is fixed regardless of meaning
misconceptions.correction: Choose the relevant sense in context.
Precision and natural use matter more than complexity.
Use the word accurately in a new context and connect it to a word network.

AC9E4LA12.title: Punctuating Dialogue
AC9E4LA12.curriculum: understand that punctuation signals dialogue through quotation marks and that dialogue follows conventions for the use of capital letters, commas and boundary punctuation

misconceptions.misconception: Comma placed outside closing quotation marks in this convention
misconceptions.correction: Place the comma before the closing quotation mark when it belongs to the speech-tag pattern.

misconceptions.misconception: Question mark followed by a capitalised tag
misconceptions.correction: The reporting clause continues the sentence: ‘?’ she asked.

misconceptions.misconception: New quotation mark for every line of wrapped text
misconceptions.correction: Wrapping on the page does not mean a new speaker.
Use reporting clauses, actions or paragraphing to identify speakers.

AC9E4LE01.title: Similar Storylines and Ideas Across Contexts
AC9E4LE01.curriculum: recognise similar storylines, ideas and relationships in different contexts in literary texts by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors

misconceptions.correction: Recurring patterns can be transformed through context, viewpoint and craft.
Compare at several levels: structure, idea, relationship and language.

misconceptions.misconception: One text represents a whole culture
misconceptions.correction: Discuss the particular representation and avoid generalisation.
Explain how it affects events, relationships or meaning.

AC9E4LE02.title: Responding to Literary Structure and Language
AC9E4LE02.curriculum: describe the effects of text structures and language features in literary texts when responding to and sharing opinions

misconceptions.misconception: Opinion counts as analysis by itself
misconceptions.correction: Name the feature, evidence and effect.
Explain what it does in this context.
Select only the relevant evidence and analyse it.
Responses can vary when they are textually supported.

AC9E4LE03.title: Character, Setting and Plot Tension
AC9E4LE03.curriculum: discuss how authors and illustrators make stories engaging by the way they develop character, setting and plot tensions

misconceptions.correction: Questions, conflict, anticipation and emotional stakes can create tension.
It creates opportunities, constraints, mood and consequences.

misconceptions.misconception: Character develops because author states a trait
misconceptions.correction: Development emerges through decisions, relationships and reactions.
It may add viewpoint, foreshadowing or contradictory evidence.

AC9E4LE04.title: Literary Devices and Deliberate Word Play
AC9E4LE04.curriculum: examine the use of literary devices and deliberate word play in literary texts, including poetry, to shape meaning

misconceptions.correction: Connect evidence to local and whole-text meaning.
Focus on noticeable sound pattern, usually at nearby stressed words.
It creates a conceptual comparison, not a literal claim.
Select devices that support a coherent effect.

AC9E4LE05.title: Creating and Editing Literary Texts
AC9E4LE05.curriculum: create and edit literary texts by developing storylines, characters and settings

misconceptions.correction: Revision addresses storyline, character, setting, pacing and clarity.
Use decisions, dialogue, reactions and relationships as evidence.
Make it influence possibilities, mood or conflict.
Foreshadowing and causal logic help a twist feel earned.

AC9E4LY01.title: Comparing Texts from Different Times
AC9E4LY01.curriculum: compare texts from different times with similar purposes and audiences to identify similarities and differences in their depictions of events

misconceptions.misconception: Older text assumed inaccurate or inferior
misconceptions.correction: Evaluate evidence and context rather than age alone.
Genre, author, medium and audience may also explain it.
Describe historical assumptions carefully while still evaluating effects.
Identify what both texts are trying to achieve before comparing form.

AC9E4LY02.title: Listening for Key Information and Building Discussion
AC9E4LY02.curriculum: listen for key points and information to carry out tasks and contribute to discussions, acknowledging another opinion, linking a response to the topic, and sharing and extending ideas and information

misconceptions.correction: Select information needed for the task or discussion purpose.
You can recognise a viewpoint before questioning or disagreeing.
Link explicitly to the prior contribution and discussion question.
Support contributions with information, examples or reasoning.

AC9E4LY03.title: Features of Imaginative, Informative and Persuasive Texts
AC9E4LY03.curriculum: identify the characteristic features used in imaginative, informative and persuasive texts to meet the purpose of the text

misconceptions.correction: Use a connected pattern.
Evidence can strengthen persuasion.
Selection and framing still shape information.
Identify dominant purpose and secondary functions.

AC9E4LY04.title: Accurate, Fluent and Self-correcting Reading
AC9E4LY04.curriculum: read different types of texts, integrating phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently, re-reading and self-correcting when needed

misconceptions.misconception: Guessing from picture or first letter
misconceptions.correction: Use the complete written word and cross-check meaning.
Accuracy, phrasing and comprehension are essential.
Noticing and repairing is a skilled reading behaviour.

misconceptions.misconception: Every unfamiliar word must be supplied by an adult
misconceptions.correction: Teach a strategic sequence and allow productive effort.

AC9E4LY05.title: Comprehension Strategies for Literal, Inferred and Evaluative Meaning
AC9E4LY05.curriculum: use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring and questioning to build literal and inferred meaning, to expand topic knowledge and ideas, and evaluate texts

misconceptions.correction: It should be reasonable and revised when evidence changes.
Explain how it deepens understanding of the text.
Prioritise central ideas and relationships.
Cite clues and reasoning.
Use explicit criteria and evidence.

AC9E4LY06.title: Creating Written and Multimodal Texts
AC9E4LY06.curriculum: plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal imaginative, informative and persuasive texts, using visual features, relevant linked ideas, complex sentences, appropriate tense, synonyms and antonyms, correct spelling of multisyllabic words and simple punctuation

misconceptions.correction: Use feedback and revision to strengthen meaning.

misconceptions.misconception: Editing begins before structure is solved
misconceptions.correction: Address large-scale ideas first to avoid polishing deleted text.

misconceptions.misconception: Visuals added after writing without purpose
misconceptions.correction: Plan modes together and connect them.

misconceptions.misconception: Complex sentence used only to sound advanced
misconceptions.correction: Use clause relationships to express precise meaning.
Check homophones, names, context and intended words.

AC9E4LY07.title: Structured Oral and Multimodal Presentations
AC9E4LY07.curriculum: plan, create, rehearse and deliver structured oral and/or multimodal presentations to report on a topic, tell a story, recount events or present an argument using subjective and objective language, complex sentences, visual features, tone, pace, pitch and volume

misconceptions.correction: Slides cue and extend the spoken message.
Volume should be audible and controlled, with variation for meaning.
Movement should direct attention, not distract.
Test timing, clarity, evidence, visuals and audience understanding.

misconceptions.misconception: Subjective language replaces evidence in an argument
misconceptions.correction: Use evaluation alongside verifiable support.

AC9E4LY08.title: Fluent and Legible Joined Handwriting
AC9E4LY08.curriculum: write words using clearly formed joined letters, with developing fluency and automaticity

misconceptions.correction: Follow the approved style; forced joins can reduce clarity.
Fluency balances pace, accuracy, comfort and legibility.
Transfer movements into words and authentic writing.
Excess tension reduces endurance and movement quality.

misconceptions.misconception: One handwriting form fits every access need
misconceptions.correction: Use suitable adjustments or digital alternatives when required.

AC9E4LY09.title: Reading and Writing Complex Multisyllabic Words
AC9E4LY09.curriculum: understand how to use and apply phonological and morphological knowledge to read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter combinations, including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes

misconceptions.misconception: Syllable and morpheme boundaries must match
misconceptions.correction: They serve different purposes and may divide differently.

misconceptions.misconception: Every vowel letter makes one sound
misconceptions.correction: Vowel graphemes and unstressed vowels can be complex.

misconceptions.misconception: Prefix guessed without checking base meaning
misconceptions.correction: Confirm that the remaining base and whole-word meaning make sense.
Context verifies a word; written evidence remains essential.

misconceptions.misconception: Word read once but not understood
misconceptions.correction: Connect pronunciation to morphology and sentence meaning.

AC9E4LY10.title: Spelling Complex Words through Patterns, Morphology and Origins
AC9E4LY10.curriculum: understand how to use knowledge of letter patterns, including double letters, spelling generalisations, morphological word families, common prefixes and suffixes, and word origins, to spell more complex words

misconceptions.correction: Doubling depends on vowel, stress and word ending conditions.
Some suffixes retain it and some words need it for pronunciation.
Morphology and origin often preserve letters not clearly heard.

misconceptions.misconception: Word origin used as a memorised trivia list
misconceptions.correction: Connect it to meaning and recurring spelling patterns.
Verify uncertain words and record useful exceptions.

AC9E4LY11.title: High-frequency Words, Homophones and Context
AC9E4LY11.curriculum: read and write high-frequency words including homophones and know how to use context to identify correct spelling

misconceptions.correction: Use meaning and grammar because homophones sound alike.
It may accept a real but contextually wrong word.
In they’re and you’re it marks omitted letters.
It’s expands to it is/has; its is possessive.
Context errors can still occur in familiar words.
